use_case: A general-purpose AI coding agent you use from the terminal, VS Code or JetBrains to read a codebase, edit files across a project, run shell commands and tests, and plan or debug changes. It can also run unattended in CI with `kilo run --auto`.
not_for: Not tied to data/SQL, DevOps or other specialist domains: it has no dedicated tools for them beyond the shell and web fetch
Not a chat assistant for non-code work: its agents (Code, Plan, Ask, Debug) are all built around a code repository
evidence: README.md:24 and 112-134 describe an open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the CLI, with Code, Plan, Ask and Debug agents, terminal and browser control, MCP support and `kilo run --auto` for CI. The tool definitions in packages/opencode/src/tool/ (read, write, edit, apply_patch, glob, grep, lsp, shell.ts, task, todowrite, webfetch, websearch, repo_clone, plan-enter/exit, skill) show it can edit files, run shell commands, spawn subagents and access the web. AGENTS.md describes the Agent Manager, which runs multiple sessions in git worktrees. I picked the languages from the repo's own TypeScript/JavaScript code and general usage; the tool prompts do not name specific languages.
